output.brief: The rejections trace to a data error in your own systems, not to the fungicide, Lower Serra growers or Meridane. When Meridane bookings moved to the new documentation suite, the mandarin product record was copied from the avocado record and kept its 7.0°C carriage temperature. Your specification is 4.0°C. All five Meridane containers were sent at 7.0°C and all five were rejected. The carrier's units held that setpoint within 0.4°C. All four containers sent at 4.0°C passed, including ones packed with the new fungicide. The carrier's records match your own loggers, so a cargo claim would fail. Suspending Lower Serra growers or going back to the old fungicide would punish the wrong party and fix nothing. Lower Serra fruit shows higher decay inside the rejected containers, but it made up only 28–40% of each container. That may be a secondary effect. It is not established. Do now: correct the temperature on the mandarin product record. Have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct to 4°C. Add a check of reefer settings against the product specification before each submission. Check other products copied from the same template. Confidence is high.
